translations.text: The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and all the families of the house of Israel.
Is Israel a slave, or was he born into slavery in the household? Why has he become plunder?

If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and becomes another man's wife, does he return to her again? Surely that land would be thoroughly defiled. Yet you have prostituted yourself with many lovers. Return to me, says the Lord.

Raise your eyes to the paths and see: where have you not been defiled? You sat along the roads waiting for them, like a raven in the wilderness. You defiled the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.
At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all the nations will look to the name of the Lord. They will no longer follow the desires of their evil hearts.
For this is what the Lord says to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Light a lamp for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.
For a voice announces news from Dan and proclaims distress from the mountain of Ephraim.
How can I forgive you? Your children have abandoned me and sworn by those that are not gods. I fed them until they were full, but they committed adultery and fought in the house of prostitutes.

Look, I am bringing a nation from far away against you, house of Israel, says the Lord. It is a mighty nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you do not understand.
The prophets prophesied falsehood, and the priests held their hands, and my people loved it that way. But what will you do in the end?
I appointed watchmen over you so that you would listen to the sound of the trumpet. But you say, 'We will not listen.'
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
They built high places at Topheth in the valley of Ben-hinnom to burn their sons and daughters in the fire, something I did not command them and that never entered my mind.
How can you say, 'We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us'? Surely the scribe's lying pen has been put to work for falsehood.
You dwell in the midst of deceit. In their deceit they refused to know me, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: Let the wise person not boast in his wisdom, let the mighty person not boast in his might, and let the rich person not boast in his riches.
Who would not fear you, King of all the ages? For kingship belongs to you. Among all the wise people of the nations and throughout all their kingdoms, there is no one like you.
Say this to them: The gods that did not make heaven and earth will perish from the earth and from beneath these heavens.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:

Which I commanded your ancestors on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said, 'Listen to my voice and do everything I command you. You will be my people, and I will be your God.'

The Lord of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you because of the wickedness that the house of Israel and the house of Judah committed, provoking me to anger by burning incense to Baal.
Lord, show me, and I will know. Truly, you have shown me their deeds.
But you, Lord, know me and have seen me and tested my heart before you. Prepare them like sheep for slaughter, and set them apart for the day of killing.
They made it desolate and ruined it. In its desolation it mourned over me. The whole land has become desolate because no one takes it to heart.

For just as a belt clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me, says the Lord, so that they would be my people, my name, my honor, and my praise. But they did not listen.

Say to them, “This is what the Lord says: Look, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with drunkenness.”
Hope of Israel and its Savior in times of distress, do not be like a foreign resident in the land, or like a traveler who turns aside to spend the night.
I said, “Please, Lord God! Look, the prophets are telling them, ‘You will not see the sword, and you will have no famine. Instead, I will give you peace and truth in this place.’”
For your name’s sake, do not be angry, and do not dishonor your glorious throne. Remember, and do not break your covenant with us.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

For this is what the Lord says: “Do not enter the house of dancing, do not go to dance, and do not sympathize with them, for I have taken away my peace from this people,” says the Lord, “along with kindness and mercy.”
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when people will no longer say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the house of Israel up from the land of Egypt.”

He will be like a tree planted beside water, firmly establishing its roots beside a stream. It will not fear when heat comes, and its leaves will flourish. In a year with little rain, it will not fear or stop producing fruit.
The heart is stronger than everything; it is human. Who knows it?
But if you truly listen to me, says the Lord, and do not bring a load through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and keep the Sabbath day holy and do no work on it,
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:
“Can I not do to you as this potter does, house of Israel?” says the Lord. “Look, as clay is in the potter’s hands, so you are in my hands, house of Israel.”

Therefore, give their children over to famine and hand them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives be bereaved and widowed, their men struck down by death, and their young men killed by the sword in battle.
Break the jar in full view of the men who go with you.
The next day, Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of confinement. Jeremiah said to him, “The Lord has not named you Pashhur, but ‘Foreign Resident and Wanderer.’”

This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: “Look, I will turn back the weapons in your hands with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who are besieging you outside the city, and I will gather them inside this city.”
I will strike the inhabitants of this city, both people and animals. They will die in a great plague.
If you truly carry out this command, kings who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this house, riding in chariots and on horses, each with his servants and his people.
But if you do not obey this command, I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a ruin.
Many nations will pass by this great city, and each person will say to his companion, “Why has the Lord done this to this great city?”
He will be buried as a donkey is buried: they will drag him away and throw him beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when people will no longer say, “As the Lord lives, who brought the house of Israel up from the land of Egypt.”
“If someone hides in a hiding place, do I not see him?” says the Lord. “Look, heaven and earth are full of me,” says the Lord Almighty.

The Lord showed me two baskets of figs placed before the Lord’s temple, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the craftsmen and metalworkers from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

“Look, I will send for and bring all the clans of the northern kingdoms,” says the Lord, “and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant. I will bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and all these surrounding nations. I will destroy them and make them an object of horror and hissing, and a ruin forever.”
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin and an object of horror and hissing, as they are to this day.
I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.
As for me, here I am in your hands. Do to me whatever seems good and right to you.
For this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says about the pillars, the Sea, the basins, and the rest of the vessels that remain in this city:
Go and tell Hananiah the false prophet: This is what the LORD says: In place of the wooden yokes you broke, make an iron yoke.
By the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in Babylon.
This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the captives who were taken from Jerusalem to Babylon:
For this is what the LORD says: Your injury is painful, and your wound is severe.
I will build you again, and you will be rebuilt, virgin Israel. Again you will adorn yourself with ornaments and go out with the gathering of those who sing praises.
I have indeed heard Ephraim lamenting and saying: You disciplined me, LORD, and I was disciplined. I was like an untamed calf. Bring me back, and I will return, for you are the LORD my God.
The measuring line will again extend straight ahead over the hill of Gareb and turn toward the hill.
Zedekiah king of Judah had imprisoned him, saying: Why do you prophesy and say, ‘This is what the LORD says: I am handing this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will conquer it’?

I gave the deeds of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, in the presence of Nahmael, my uncle’s son, and in the presence of the witnesses whose names were written on the deeds of purchase, and in the presence of all the Jews who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
This is what the LORD says, who made you, formed you, and established you—the LORD is his name:

This is what the LORD says: Again there will be heard in this place, which you say is desolate, without people or livestock—in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, which are desolate, without people, inhabitants, or livestock:
For this is what the LORD says: David will never lack a son to sit on the throne of the house of Israel.

Instead, you will die in peace. As they mourned for your ancestors, the former kings who came before you, so they will mourn for you. They will lament over you, ‘Alas, master!’ For I have spoken this word, says the LORD.

King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought up. The king questioned him secretly in the palace and said to him, ‘Has a word come from the LORD?’ Jeremiah said, ‘It has.’ The king said, ‘What word has come?’ He said, ‘You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.’
My lord, these men have done wrong in everything they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they threw into the pit. Look, he is dying of hunger, because there is no bread in the city.
Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, left some of the poor people who had nothing in the land of Judah, and on that day he gave them vineyards and fields.
The captain of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, ‘The LORD your God pronounced disaster against this place.’
All the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned back and came to Johanan son of Kareah.
After ten days, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet.

For this is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Just as my anger and fury came to rest upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my fury will come to rest upon you when you enter Egypt. You will become an object of oaths, horror, cursing, and disgrace, and you will never see this place again.

He will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt, burn them, and take them captive. He will wrap the land around himself as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will leave there in peace.

That fragrant incense which you offered in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem—you, your ancestors, your kings, your officials, and the people of the land—the LORD remembered it, and it came to his mind.
This is what the LORD Almighty, the God of Israel, says: Take up weapons and shields, and advance to battle.
The nations have heard of your disgrace, and your wailing has filled the earth, because one man has stumbled against another, and both have fallen by the sword.
Declare it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, and proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes. Say, “Prepare yourselves and stand ready, because the sword has devoured those around you.”
Pack your belongings for captivity, virgin daughter of Egypt, because Memphis will become a ruin and lie desolate, without anyone living there.

The Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says, “Look, I am bringing punishment upon Amon of the waters, upon Pharaoh, upon Egypt, upon her gods, upon her army, upon her kings, upon Pharaoh, and upon everyone who trusts in him.”
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, telling him to prophesy against the Philistines before Pharaoh struck Gaza.
Moab is ashamed because it has been shattered. Wail and cry out in Arnon, because Moab has been shattered.
We have heard of the leaders of Moab, who are very proud—their pride, their arrogance, and the haughtiness of their hearts.
Look, he will rise and soar like an eagle and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman suffering the pains of childbirth.
Damascus has grown weak and turned to flee. Trembling has seized her; distress and pains have gripped her like a woman giving birth.

“I will shatter Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger,” says the Lord. “I will send the sword among them until I have destroyed them.”

For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon assemblies of many nations from the northern land. They will draw up their battle lines against her, and from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like a successful warrior who does not return empty-handed.
Because of the Lord’s anger, she will not be inhabited but will be entirely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
The sound of those fleeing and escaping from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, vengeance for his temple.
Therefore her troops will fall within her, and all her fighting men will be silenced on that day.
She will be like Sodom and Gomorrah, which God overthrew along with their inhabitants. No one will live there, and no human being will settle there.
The king of Babylon has heard the report about them, and his hands have gone limp. Distress has seized him, and pains like those of a woman giving birth.
For this is what the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, says: “The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor when the time has come to tread it. In a little while her harvest will come.”

Jerusalem said, “Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has devoured me and plundered me. He has left me like an empty vessel. He has swallowed me like a dragon, filled his belly with my delicacies, and driven me away.”
“I will make her leaders, her wise men, her nobles, her rulers, and her warriors drunk. They will sleep forever and will not awaken,” says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.
Jeremiah wrote in one scroll all the disaster that was coming upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, “When you enter Babylon, read and examine all these words.”
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, and he pronounced judgment on him.
